hazards.evidence: Pet bowl and a small soft object (toy/slipper) on the carpet right beside the bed, in the area where a walker user would step/stand.
Narrow gap between the side of the bed and the adjacent wall (where the outlet/night light and bowl sit) appears too tight to position and turn a walker safely at the bedside.
Bed looks relatively low for post hip/knee replacement transfers; mattress top appears near or below knee height, making sit-to-stand with a walker harder.
Walking route from the bed toward the doorway is narrowed by the bed on one side and the swung-open door/dresser on the other, with items on the floor.
Only a low plug-in night light and a far bedside lamp; the bed-to-door route and far hallway are dim, which is risky for night-time walker trips.
Carpeted bedroom floor meets a different floor surface at the doorway/hallway with a visible threshold edge that is not marked.
Pet feeding bowl and a small pet toy/soft item left on the floor in the bedside walkway are underfoot trip hazards for a walker user.
The open bedroom door and frame leave a narrowed clear opening; a standard walker may have limited clearance passing through, especially with the door swinging into the path.
